subject.title: [Bug]: Codex runtime collapses automatic WhatsApp reply blocks into one bubble

question: Should newline mode continue to pack short adjacent paragraphs up to the channel limit, or should it become a cross-runtime policy that preserves each blank-line paragraph as a separate outbound send?
rationale: Current main intentionally implements packing, while the active linked PR would change visible delivery semantics across all applicable channels; source cannot determine which user-facing contract maintainers want to support.

options.title: Retain packed newline sends
options.body: Keep the current shared contract, where short adjacent paragraphs may be combined until the transport limit is reached.

options.title: Adopt preserved paragraph sends
options.body: Approve a deliberate shared outbound-policy change and require upgrade-focused tests and proof across the affected delivery paths.

recommendation.title: Retain packed newline sends
recommendation.body: Keep the current shared contract, where short adjacent paragraphs may be combined until the transport limit is reached.

likelyOwner.reason: The current behavior appears to originate in their merged shared outbound chunking work, making them the strongest history-based routing candidate.
